title: Truncation preserves negative evaluations
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\varphi$ be a DNF formula on $n$ sign coordinates, let $w\in\mathbb N$, and let $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. If the DNF obtained from $\varphi$ by retaining only terms of width at most $w$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$, then $\varphi$ itself evaluates to $-1$ at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $\varphi$ is a DNF formula on $n$ coordinates
The width-$w$ truncation of $\varphi$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$
